subject: Hosted baseline delta: tiering, discounts & private deployment implications

Subject: Request: baseline hosted rates + delta to Dedicated/Private

Karthik —

Thanks for taking this. We're trying to map out cost expectations for a multi-product rollout (chat, embeddings, reranking) and need a clear baseline for Hosted API unit rates and how those change when moving to Dedicated or Private. Specific asks:

- Hosted baseline per-token rates (or per-1k-token bucket) for small/medium/large workloads (estimates are fine)
- Typical discount ranges for committed monthly/annual Dedicated (1yr / 3yr)
- One-time platform/private deployment fees (on-prem licensing, support SLA addons)
- Any packaging levers (burst to Hosted from Dedicated, shared KV cache, hybrid routing) that materially change economics

I've attached our internal rate request template for your team to fill (Finovate_rate_request.xlsx). Would also appreciate an example pricing sketch for a 12-month commitment at ~120B tokens/month and a second scenario with burst patterns (spiky usage).

Happy to do a 30-min call if easier — procurement is looped here.

Daniel —

Thanks for the clear ask and the template — that's helpful. High level answers up front so you can unblock procurement:

- Hosted baseline: we publish per-token bands; for a quick sketch, think of Hosted as the reference price (no upfront), with unit reductions driven by volume tiers and committed usage.
- Dedicated: Reserved GPU capacity with commit -> typical material discounts versus Hosted because of capacity reservation and lower per-token OS overhead.
- Private: Combines a platform fee + optional reserved capacity. Expect a license/platform uplift but lower per-token if you take dedicated GPU pools on-prem or in your VPC for sustained high throughput.

I'll have Neha pull together a concise delta table + example scenarios (120B tokens/mo and spiky burst). I've attached a short internal summary and will convert to your template.

Propose a 30-min sync Wed 11/4 to walk the scenarios. Marcus — can you confirm whether Marketplace procurement (GCP/AWS) could be in scope here (proc and billing implications)?

Best,

Subject: Re: Request: baseline hosted rates + delta to Dedicated/Private

Daniel / team —

Filling in the delta table here (high-level bullets; I'll attach a filled worksheet by EOD):

- Hosted baseline: reference per-token bands; simplest packaging — pay-as-you-go with volume tier stepping. Good for variable workloads and short pilots.

- Dedicated (Reserved capacity):
  - Cost drivers: committed GPU hours/instances, support tier, and capacity utilization.
  - Typical discount ranges: ~15–30% off Hosted baseline for 12mo reserved commitments; 25–45% for 36mo depending on minimum commit and utilization guarantees.
  - Operational differences: lower per-token inference overhead (no multi-tenant throttling), ability to tune quantization/batching resulting in further effective cost reduction for high throughput workloads.

- Private (VPC / on-prem):
  - Components: one-time private platform license / onboarding fee, optional managed-support retainer, and either Dedicated-like reserved capacity or self-managed infra.
  - Economics: per-token can be lower than Hosted if you provision and utilize dedicated GPUs; however, platform fee and professional services make short-term ROI worse for pilots. For sustained >100B tokens/mo, Private can be the lowest unit cost over a multi-year horizon.

- Packaging levers that change economics materially:
  1) Commit length (12 vs 36 mo) — biggest lever for Dedicated discounts.
  2) Burst policies — keep a small Dedicated pool + burst to Hosted; reduces committed spend but preserves tail capacity.
  3) Shared prefix/KV caching — reduces served tokens for repeat prompts; very effective for chat-heavy workloads.
  4) Quantization & batching profiles — we recommend 8-bit/4-bit where quality allows; tooling in Redwood Optimize can show estimated savings.

I'll populate exact sketch numbers for your two scenarios (120B steady + spiky pattern) and upload to your template.

-Neha

Quick note from GTM/finance side —

- Procurement sometimes expects a simple single-line discount versus Hosted to simplify vendor comparisons. For a first pass we can offer: "Hosted baseline - 18% for 12mo committed Dedicated + standard SRE support" as a negotiable starter. This assumes a minimum commit (e.g., 80–100B tokens/mo equivalent) and a standard SLA.
- Marketplace (GCP/AWS): if they purchase via Marketplace, we typically have to factor in platform fees and marketplace reseller cut; that reduces our room to discount, so direct billing is preferred for larger committed deals.
- Packaging we should propose: (A) Pure Hosted pilot for 3 months, (B) 12mo Dedicated commit with burst-to-hosted and 1-time private onboarding option. That maps cleanly to their asks and preserves upgrade path.

Karthik — can you confirm we want to signal that upper bound (18%) or keep it as "up to 20% dependent on term & commit" before Laura's sign-off?

Marcus Lin
Director, Commercial Strategy
marcus.lin@redwood.com

- Approve "up to 18%" off Hosted baseline for a 12-month Dedicated commit if Finovate signs for at least 90B tokens/month equivalent and accepts standard SRE response SLAs and a software support add-on.
- If Finovate requests >18%, escalate to me with their counter and a two-line TCO justification (expected token volumes + targeted latency/availability requirements).
- Marcus: include marketplace impact language in the quote (explicit callout that marketplace purchases may change net economics).

Karthik — send the updated worksheet to Daniel and procurement with the two scenarios Neha is building and the commercial language above. Copy me on the quote.
